Many tech giants are eager to pay for these upgrades to power AI. Increasing production from existing nuclear plants will add an estimated 6,000 to 8,000 megawatts of electric capacity to US grids.
items.title: A New Trend in Nuclear Energy: Squeezing More Power Out of Old Plants (7 minute read)

The DOE will invest more than $500 million across five years in lab measurement, modeling, and computation to build an AI-ready open data resource; the NIH will coordinate the contribution of relevant datasets, repositories, and knowledge bases; and Biohub will work with the NIH to standardize the datasets for AI model training.

items.summary_html: Two independent teams in Vienna and Beijing have simultaneously built the first clocks that keep time by counting the squishing and unsquishing of the atomic nuclei of thorium. The clocks are so precise that they only lose one second once every few million years or so. Nuclear clocks have the ability to search for certain kinds of dark matter. If a particle of dark matter passes through the thorium nuclei, it could register as a wobble in the nuclear clock's otherwise steady tick-tock.
items.title: In Vienna and Beijing, the First Nuclear Clocks Begin to Tick (6 minute read)

The article compares four storage patterns and argues that message appends can return the full response so far, continue live delivery, and save only the completed message to application storage.
items.title: A Token Is Not a Message: Stop Storing AI Responses Like Event Logs (21 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cortex replaced a Lucene-based search architecture with PostgreSQL full-text search, a custom query parser, weighted ranking, and CDC-fed indexes. The change cut public API p95 latency from 13.3 seconds to 1.54 seconds, reduced total memory use by about 40%, and made most edits searchable within seconds.
items.title: A Hitchhiker's Guide to Postgres Text Search (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: Software blogs lose readers when they meander, assume too much background knowledge, or outsource key explanations to links. The guide recommends stating the payoff in the title and opening sentences, writing for a specific reader, and keeping external references optional.
items.title: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Chrome 155 will ship a memory-safe JPEG XL decoder built in Rust, reversing the browser's earlier decision to remove support. Chrome's reach could make the format mainstream, especially for high-fidelity photography, lossless compression, progressive decoding, and lossless JPEG transcoding.
items.title: JPEG XL Finally Lands in Chrome! (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: The essay examines five objections to AI coding: code as art, job displacement, dehumanizing work, rule-based views of software engineering, and support for powerful AI companies. It argues that several critiques depend on debatable assumptions about what software work is for, while locating the strongest human concern in labor relations and control of production.
items.title: Reasons to Dislike AI Coding (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: GPT-6 is rolling out in ChatGPT with Intelligent UI, which can combine text, graphics, forms, charts, and interactive tools in a response. Paid tiers use GPT-6 Sol, Free and Go use GPT-6 Luna, and the release can begin responding while it continues reasoning or searching.
items.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for Everyone (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude Haiku 5.5 targets high-volume, latency-sensitive work such as summarization, classification, browser use, and subagent tasks. Anthropic says average running costs are about 75% lower than Haiku 4.5, with adjustable effort and availability across its platform, AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure.
items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 (Website)

items.summary_html: Docker Agent is a CLI plugin for defining and running AI agents from declarative YAML. It supports multi-agent orchestration, MCP and built-in tools, multiple model providers, retrieval, and packaging agents to OCI registries.
items.title: Docker Agent (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Agentic development changes the ideal linter because automated checks run on nearly every coding turn and agents can act on rules that humans might find too noisy. Ultracite pairs fast tools such as Oxlint and Oxfmt with strict rules and agent instructions, while keeping judgment-heavy questions for review.
items.title: The Agentic Development Loop (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: A remote Upstash Box gives Grok Bot a shell, persistent filesystem, GitHub integration, public previews, schedules, snapshots, and optional browser automation through MCP. The examples show it building a live app, cloning and fixing repositories, and turning a Slack report into a Linear ticket and pull request from a phone.
items.title: I Gave Grok Bot a Remote Computer (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Vanguard's password reset form silently truncated pasted passwords at 20 characters, while its login form accepted the full value and then rejected it as incorrect. The incident shows why password length limits should be validated visibly in JavaScript or on the server instead of using an HTML maxlength attribute that changes the submitted credential.
items.title: input type="password" maxlength="20" Prevents Me from Logging into Vanguard (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Firestore-to-SQL migration only became faster after the read model moved aggregation to the server, cutting a ten-year view from 56 seconds to 3.7 seconds and shrinking the shared search payload from 18.27 MB to 1.63 MB.
items.title: We Moved Off Firestore. The Slow Page Stayed Slow (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: This visual notation distinguishes React's parent and owner trees so component structure and creation relationships can be read as diagrams instead of inferred from scattered code.
items.title: A Visual Notation for React's Parent and Owner Trees (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Size Limit enforces JavaScript performance budgets in CI, including bundle size, dependency cost, and estimated download and execution time.
items.title: Size Limit (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: REA connects coding agents to local tools for reverse engineering websites, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and native binaries.
items.title: REA (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: PostHog describes the shared runtime behind its Desktop, Slack, self-driving, and web agents, built around Temporal workflows, VM sandboxes, snapshots, fresh credentials, and resumable run logs. The hard-won lessons cover queued follow-ups, deterministic network controls, Docker-capable custom images, and designing every run to survive the loss of its sandbox.
items.title: We built our own cloud agents runtime. Here's what we learned (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: A reverse-engineering tour traces ChatGPT's interactive responses from a model-written DIL format through server-side compilation, sandboxed client execution, and native rendering. It also explains how streaming recompiles partial output, preserves keyed state, and sends server-resolved data such as images separately from model text.
items.title: How ChatGPT Intelligent UI works (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: An investigation of Chrome's experimental Decisions API compares the explainer with implementation code and review comments. It surfaces slow Gemma 4 timings, position bias, context limits, probability semantics, and differences between Chrome's prototype and MediaPipe's DecisionMaker.
items.title: Chrome Decisions API: the prompts, limits, engines and code reviews behind DecisionModel (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: As AI makes code production cheap, the scarce work shifts to choosing priorities, reviewing product behavior, maintaining architecture, and owning outcomes in production. Senior engineers create leverage by turning repeated review feedback into guidance and deterministic lint rules while keeping human judgment for business context.
items.title: When code is cheap, judgement becomes the job (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: A practical test gate checks agent-written changes on a clean machine before review by reinstalling from scratch, running the full suite three times, rejecting removed or skipped tests, and restoring the base branch's tests against the new code. Running the same gate inside the agent loop turns failures into immediate repair instructions while an independent CI run keeps the verdict outside the agent's control.
items.title: Don't merge what you didn't run: a test gate for agent-written code (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Treg acts as an OpenRouter for agent tools, giving agents one base URL and token for a catalog of metered provider endpoints plus team-owned APIs, CLIs, and skills. It can inject credentials server-side, expose tools through MCP and agent skills, and let teams share capabilities without placing provider keys in callers.
items.title: Treg (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Plannotator provides a local browser-based review surface for plans, Markdown, HTML artifacts, diffs, and pull requests produced by coding agents. Hooks and commands route annotations back to agents, with support for multiple agent harnesses and local-first storage by default.
items.title: Plannotator (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A React Server Components flaw let an attacker force quadratic work while React rebuilt FormData for a server action, allowing a roughly 900 KB request to trigger 100 million string checks and block a Node.js event loop. The issue affects vulnerable React 19.0 to 19.2 releases and is fixed in 19.0.6, 19.1.7, and 19.2.6.
items.title: A Single POST Freezes Any Next.js Server (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Expo built a CI evaluation harness that measures whether coding agents discover relevant skills, follow their guidance, and produce working apps. Adding an overview skill raised sessions loading at least one downstream Expo skill from 9% to 55%, while catalog crowding tests showed why names and opening descriptions must survive truncation.
items.title: Your skills need an evaluation mechanism (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: The origin story of Zotero shows how years of conversation, prototypes, and collaboration helped a team of historians discover what durable research software should become. Its path from Web Scrapbook and Scribe to a browser-aware tool used by millions argues that clear product vision can require slow communal formation, even when implementation itself becomes cheap.
items.title: The Slow Formation of Durable Software (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: calc-input lets forms accept arithmetic expressions, shows formulas on focus and results on blur, and uses a safe parser plus native form validation instead of eval().
items.title: calc-input, a custom input element that accepts mathematical formulas (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Google study found most internal open source package updates take four hours or less, while local patches, dependencies, and upstream contributor counts better predicted difficult updates than package age or internal adoption.
items.title: How much does it cost to use open source software? (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: A display-only flicker that browser captures could not reproduce was traced to full-width tile repaints, then reduced from 267 page-tile repaints to 9 by promoting only the changing timeline elements to their own composited layers.
items.title: The Bug Only My Screen Could See (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: video-shotcraft turns coding agents into a Remotion-based motion studio with 157 shot recipes, 214 motion previews, editable templates, sound design guidance, and a browser workbench.
items.title: video-shotcraft (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A Qwen3-1.7B walkthrough turns multiple-choice questions into single-pass predictions by scoring only the allowed answer tokens. Fine-tuning improves accuracy on a 1,221-question CommonsenseQA sample from 59.4% to 62.4%, while temperature scaling makes the model's confidence better reflect its actual accuracy.
items.title: Build Your Own Decision Model (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Three production investigations, a latency regression, a memory leak, and a kernel-level hang, show how to steer coding agents through unfamiliar systems using runtime evidence. The framework separates facts from hypotheses, compares failures with a control, and requires every proposed cause to satisfy all known constraints. Adversarial reviews should seek contradictions, and reproductions must match the real failure's signals before they can be trusted.
items.title: How to Effectively Debug When You No Longer Understand the Code (63 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cockroach Labs structures coding agents around a teaching hospital, with reviewed plans, separate implementation and review roles, structured handoffs, and an audit before merge. The pipeline landed over a million lines of code in five months with seven reverts, and human approval became mandatory after the first autonomous week before the team used it to build customer-facing migration tooling.
items.title: Five Months Treating Bugs Like Patients and Coding Agents Like a Medical Team (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: The AI-generated Campfire app rewrites make different choices about compatibility, queues, and concurrency, so throughput alone cannot establish which language performs better. Constant-arrival-rate tests expose tradeoffs between dropped notifications, timeouts, memory use, and delivery latency, showing why engineers still need to inspect code and specify failure behavior.
items.title: I'm Sorry, but You Still Have to Think (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: A personal reflection explores the loss of professional identity when AI shifts attention from low-level knowledge and performance details toward architecture and delegation.
items.title: Grieving the Loss of Details (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: An account of using DeepSeek 4.1 Flash across a dozen projects argues that inexpensive models can handle much of the work typically assigned to premium frontier models. Lower session costs encourage unattended chores, exploratory testing, and long planning sessions, with a more expensive model sometimes brought in for a final review.
items.title: Why Isn't the Industry Freaking Out About DeepSeek 4.1 Flash? (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A macOS command-line tool lets coding agents draw temporary arrows, boxes, and text over the screen to show users where to click. Its transparent overlays allow clicks through to the underlying application and disappear automatically, with skills provided for Claude Code and Codex.
items.title: Big Arrow on the Screen (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: REA gives coding agents tools to reverse engineer native binaries, JavaScript and Electron applications, and browser behavior. Its examples recover Windows Calculator's percentage rules and a browser game's acceleration logic, then use those findings to explain or rebuild the features.
items.title: REA (Website)

items.summary_html: Talorys is a single-user personal AI assistant that runs in your own Cloudflare account and deploys with one command. It combines chat, editable memory, tasks, notes, projects, and scheduled reminders, with core organizational features continuing to work when AI is unavailable.
items.title: Talorys (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: A MonetDB count-distinct query saturates an NVMe drive with writes because Linux flushes dirty pages from temporary memory-mapped scratch files. Moving the scratch files to tmpfs cuts runtime from 73 minutes to 97 seconds, while workload-specific writeback tuning reaches about 100 seconds without moving them off disk.
items.title: The Dirty Pages Surprise: When a Read-Only Query Writes Terabytes (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: Speculative decoding accelerates generation by drafting several tokens cheaply and verifying them in one target-model pass while preserving the target's output distribution. This detailed walkthrough derives acceptance and speedup formulas, covers EAGLE-3, multi-token prediction, and diffusion drafters, and explains why training for acceptance is different from simply minimizing KL divergence.
items.title: Speculative Decoding: The Art of Guessing Well (70 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Deno team is joining Cloudflare to focus on a shared platform built around Workers, Durable Objects, and celld. Deno runtime development will end after one year of bug fixes and security updates, Deno Deploy will shut down in six months, and JSR will continue operating on Cloudflare infrastructure.
items.title: Deno Is Joining Cloudflare (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: In a PostgreSQL 18 laptop benchmark loading 10 million rows, UUIDv7 took 32.3 seconds versus 29.7 for bigint and 60.7 for UUIDv4.
items.title: PostgreSQL uuidv7 Keys Load Like bigint, UUIDv4 Took Twice as Long (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Git commit storage depends on directory structure, filesystem overhead, and compression.
items.title: How Big Is a Git Commit? (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft-Decision-1 scores fixed answer options in a single pass for routing, classification, and workflow control.
items.title: Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, Our Model for Fast Decision-Making (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Human and AI teams may remain the strongest software builders for another decade or two.
items.title: Software's Centaur Age May Last Decades (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google's DevSite stored an OAuth secret inside a readable Flask session cookie and reused it as the cookie's signing key, allowing forged sessions to reach unsafe pickle deserialization. Timing-based tests confirmed unauthenticated code execution across the shared platform, earning a $90,000 bounty. The fix separates signing keys from OAuth credentials and removes sensitive serialized objects from client-controlled sessions.
items.title: How I Found a $90,000 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in Google (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: React Compiler uses cache slots and tracks values that change together to avoid unnecessary work. In a 2,000-row microbenchmark, inlining alone slowed rendering from 444 ms to 1,038 ms by removing per-row caches, while adding block DOM updates cut it to 164 ms. These prototypes illustrate optimization opportunities, with workload and memory tradeoffs still to evaluate.
items.title: Can we Make React Faster using the React Compiler? (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Perplexity Projects uses a lightweight Git forge backed by S3 storage so people and agents can build on durable files from isolated, temporary sandboxes. Submissions must match the latest accepted commit, with stale writers replaying their changes rather than overwriting concurrent work. In production, fewer than 2% of submissions are rejected as stale, with median submit latency below 1.7 seconds.
items.title: Building Shared Workspaces for People and Agents (10 minute read)

items.summary_html: AI code review will increasingly replace reading every diff, shifting human work toward requirements, acceptance testing, and ownership of releases. Independent review models, predefined guardrails, and automated review-and-fix cycles form the proposed safety net. A trading-bot rounding bug illustrates the tradeoff: fast fixes do not erase losses or compensate for gaps in the specification.
items.title: Human PR Review Is Next (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: WebMCP lets websites expose JavaScript tools to agents, reducing the slow, brittle interaction of navigating through screenshots and DOM inspection while keeping users in a shared browser session. Shopify's checkout experiment reported 2.7 times faster execution, 58% lower cost, and 60 successful attempts out of 60 compared with 56 for browser automation. Permissions, human approval signals, and testing against complete agent systems remain open challenges.
items.title: Why WebMCP Matters (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: PostHog's lessons from ten AI products emphasize useful jobs, reliable execution, rich context, and interfaces that let agents do everything users can. Its MCP server has five times as many daily users as PostHog AI, while the install wizard compresses roughly two hours of setup into eight minutes. The advice favors shared infrastructure, observable tool calls, small targeted evals, and UI for reviewing and undoing agent actions.
items.title: 38 Things We've Learned About Building AI Products (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: Meta introduces Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full for coding and other long-running tasks, combining Active Memory for retrieving relevant context with Active Focus for sustained execution. Meta reports stronger performance on unfamiliar tasks from larger base models and plans a fuller safety report.
items.title: Muse Wonder: A Frontier Model for Personal & Professional AI Agents (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Open Intelligent UI is an open-source chat interface built with CopilotKit and AG-UI that turns questions into explanations, comparisons, and interactive tools. Its agent chooses text, native components, or custom HTML, CSS, and JavaScript rendered in an isolated iframe, with Jev routing tables to A2UI and richer visuals to Open Generative UI.
items.title: Open Intelligent UI (GitHub Repo)

items.summary_html: Vals AI tested politically sensitive questions across languages and contexts, finding that Chinese models sometimes criticize China's government while non-Chinese models sometimes echo official narratives. Responses generally leaned more pro-China in Simplified Chinese, while deployment prompts, response formats, and agent harnesses could substantially change the results.
items.title: How Pro-China Are Chinese Models? (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic demonstrates a 26B model running across 15 inexpensive Android TV boxes and a 9B model setting up inference on eight of nine tested hardware types. GLM-5.2 completed replication in a contained fleet with deliberately trivial access controls, making the result an upper bound on real-world success. Smaller models still struggle to chain the steps together, while projected replication on low-powered devices would take days.
items.title: AI Models May Be Capable of Self-Replicating Without Access to a Datacenter (26 minute read)

items.summary_html: Explicit, repetitive Ruby code can make algorithms easy to inspect and resemble the optimized output of ERB and Papercraft template compilers. A proposed quote/unquote mechanism would let Ruby generate code by composing immutable syntax trees instead of concatenating source strings, with examples covering memoization, templates, and routing.
items.title: Unrolled Code (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: vlt reduces registry metadata by keeping install-time fields that npm's abbreviated format omits and removing signature, checksum, and attestation data while retaining tarball integrity checks.
items.title: How we made registry metadata 70% smaller (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Django newsletter archive took shape through a half-hour voice conversation with Codex while dinner cooked, followed by another half-hour of typed review and refinements before deployment.
items.title: I Built a New Feature for My Blog Using My Voice (27 minute read)

items.summary_html: Falling cost per task, increasingly capable open models, and on-device inference raise questions about frontier labs' pricing power and whether their infrastructure spending can support durable businesses.
items.title: This Year's Model (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: The browser already supplies much of an agent platform's identity, isolation, and user control, while WebMCP needs clearer agent permissions, operations that survive navigation, human handoffs, and coordination among assistants.
items.title: The Next Steps on the Web and WebMCP (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Mistral Large 4 is a one-trillion-parameter multimodal model positioned as a European alternative to leading closed and open AI systems.
items.title: Mistral Large 4 (9 minute read)

items.summary_html: Nano Banana 2.1 is a member of the Gemini 3 series of models. It can take text and image inputs and output images and text. Based on Gemini 3.6 Flash, the model has a token context window of up to 1 million. Nano Banana 2.1 is available in the Gemini app and API, Google AI Studio, Google Search AI Mode, Google Ads, Google Flow, and Google Stitch.
items.title: Nano Banana 2.1 (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI has released a broad range of mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model. It has published the results in a GitHub repository along with protocols for paper revisions and citations. The repository contains formalizations of many of the proofs in Lean and will be updated with more formalizations as they are obtained. It also includes 10 summaries of the model's reasoning, estimations of compute spent in terms of Pro usage on ChatGPT, and statistics about the number of attempted problems.
items.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Open-weight models potentially pose an untenable risk to society's functionality. Chinese companies continue to release open-weight models with strong cyber capabilities. GLM-5.3 crosses a threshold of capability, but there is little public evidence that much has changed. Some say that open-weight models will result in a crippling of cyber infrastructure - after many years of debating open-weight risks, we will finally start to get some real answers.
items.title: The Cyber Risk Discourse is Broken (11 minute read)

items.summary_html: Google Project Zero examined how large software vendors can patch urgent vulnerabilities faster than their normal release cycles allow. The guide breaks down the full remediation pipeline (from triage and development through testing, delivery, and activation) and highlights systems designed for exceptional security incidents.
items.title: Building Faster Emergency Patching Systems (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's Decisions API is now available to all developers in public beta. It makes decisions up to 10 times faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. The Decisions API accepts text and image inputs and supports three kinds of outputs: predicates, choices, and scores. It costs $0.10 per 1 million input tokens - there are no cache-read, cache-write, or output-token charges.
items.title: Decisions API is now available in Public Beta (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: EmbeddingGemma 2 is a 740M-parameter model that maps text, code, images, audio, and video into a shared embedding space. Built for on-device inference and released under Apache 2.0, it enables multimodal search and retrieval without sending data to the cloud.
items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2 (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Personal Agent Protocol is an open standard that Meta and Sierra are developing along with other industry partners. It is designed to handle authentication, empower consumers, and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs, or company agents. Consumers decide what access to give their personal agents, and companies set parameters for what those agents can do. The protocol is open for anyone to implement.
items.title: Introducing Personal Agent Protocol (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Pantheon rapidly assembled a robust UMI data collection operation, creating a diverse dataset to improve dexterous manipulation in robotics. They built custom infrastructure and hardware, drastically reducing data collection costs from $60/hr to $10/hr while ensuring data diversity. By incorporating innovative freeform and scripted methodologies, Pantheon accumulated over a million unique tasks, overcoming traditional data limitations for enhanced AI model training.
items.title: Building the Most Diverse UMI Dataset in Robotics (16 minute read)

items.summary_html: China has made recruiting the world's best scientists a national priority. It introduced a visa for scientists and is offering lucrative research grants. Foreigners are not coming despite those efforts. The number of Chinese scientists working in the US has risen rather than declined.
items.title: In Race With US, China Struggles to Recruit Foreign AI Researchers (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: TLDR is hiring its first PM to help build the agent-first operating layer used across the company. We're looking for a builder who has shipped real products/systems with LLMs. Click here to learn more.
items.title: Product Manager, Applied AI at TLDR ($225k base + $60k bonus, Fully Remote)

items.summary_html: DeepSeek is nearing a $12 billion raise, surpassing its initial 50 billion yuan target, with Tencent and CATL as major contributors. The funding boost follows the release of DeepSeek's latest AI model, with expectations it might reach 100 billion yuan. The company is also preparing for a potential Shanghai STAR Market IPO, employing CITIC Securities for assistance.
items.title: A $12B DeepSeek Raise Is Reportedly Close, With Tencent And CATL Among Backers (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude now integrates with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides for all paid plans, allowing direct editing within files.
items.title: Claude now works with Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, a Chinese AI model, now leads in agentic coding benchmarks, surpassing US competitors.
items.title: US-China AI Gap Hits 3%, and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Now Leads on Agentic Coding Benchmarks (12 minute read)

items.title: Hark debuts an AI agent a year before its first devices (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA's AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) v1.0 offers version-locked, validated recipes for stable GPU-accelerated Kubernetes cluster configurations.
items.title: AICR v1.0: Open, stable, and verifiable GPU cluster configuration (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic expanded its Cyber Verification Program into three access tiers for qualifying security professionals, providing its most capable models with reduced cyber blocking.
items.title: Anthropic Expands Verified Access to Cyber Capabilities (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenAI's GPT-6 introduces Intelligent UI to 1.2 billion ChatGPT users, enhancing responses with text, visuals, and interactive elements. It combines UI with data for dynamic, custom responses, and improves answer quality for complex queries. GPT-6 also features enhanced safety, ensuring better risk recognition and adherence to safeguards.
items.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Claude Haiku 5.5 is optimized for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks, offering lower operating costs and faster performance for applications like summaries and customer support. The model provides significant pricing advantages, being 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 for tasks involving prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Enhanced safety and cybersecurity safeguards make Haiku 5.5 more secure, with broader availability across major cloud platforms like AWS and Azure.
items.title: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Elon Musk's Grok Bot will integrate Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, and Suno, expanding beyond SpaceX's AI models to optimize task outcomes. This update follows reports of access issues with Grok on mobile and web. Grok Bot competes with personal AI agents like Meta's Muse, despite privacy concerns from some early users.
items.title: Grok Bot will use Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, and Suno, says Musk (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: The Perplexity team launched PPLX-EMBED-V2-LATE, providing multi-vector, multimodal embeddings that enable richer retrieval across text and images. These models retain token-level vectors and utilize a shared embedding space, leading to improved retrieval on benchmarks like ViDoRe(V3). Available in two sizes, 0.6B and 9B, they offer industry-leading performance for various retrieval tasks while maintaining efficiency.
items.title: Multimodal embeddings beyond a single vector (17 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anthropic isn't very transparent about its corporate structure. It is in the public's interest for the company to be transparent about who controls and governs increasingly capable AI models. This article looks at what is publicly known about Anthropic's corporate structure. It focuses on the aspects relevant to control of Anthropic's business rather than the parts that are only about economic benefits.
items.title: Anthropic's corporate structure (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Liquid AI released two new open-weight decision models, d1-3B and d1-OMNI-600M, available on Hugging Face.
items.title: Open d1: Edge decision models for text, vision, and audio (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenDocRouter is a platform for document-to-Markdown parsing using the latest open-source and frontier models. Each model runs a versioned recipe consisting of prompts, processing, and settings. The API accepts PDFs, PNG, JPEG, or URLs to those file formats. Users can toggle between synchronous responses, where the result is returned directly, and asynchronous responses, where a job is created that requires polling.
items.title: Introducing OpenDocRouter: every document model under one API (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: This paper presents a benchmark for evaluating intuitive visual reasoning capabilities in multimodal models.
items.title: Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Broadcom has been working to arrange more than $50 billion in financing for OpenAI's custom AI chip. Apollo and Blackstone are among the lenders Broadcom has talked to about participating in the deal. Oracle is separately in talks with Apollo and Goldman Sachs to arrange money for a big purchase of chips. SpaceX has talked to lenders in recent days about a $40 billion chip financing for Nvidia chips.
items.title: Oracle, Broadcom, and SpaceX Seek Blockbuster Debt Deals to Pay for AI Chips (7 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tony Fadell highlights the failure of early AI gadgets like the Rabbit R1, citing their inability to address real consumer needs and establish trust. Meta's recent AI assistant, Muse, faced security issues, showing the challenge of securing personal AI. Fadell suggests that successful AI assistants must operate on-device for privacy, with Apple being well-positioned due to its hardware and consumer trust, despite lacking a proprietary AI model.
items.title: Tony Fadell on why the first wave of AI gadgets failed — and what comes next (6 minute read)

items.summary_html: Texas paused issuing new data center permits due to its overwhelmed grid and speculative projects filling its approval queue. The state aims to ensure projects can support their grid upgrades and align with community needs regarding resources like water and noise. To manage demand, Texas is considering allowing data centers to bring their own power on-site or increase flexibility with grid connections to address capacity constraints.
items.title: Why Texas Is Making Data Centers Wait (29 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA and Microsoft announced a collaboration to integrate AI agents into Windows PCs, leveraging RTX Spark technology and Microsoft's new Execution Containers for securely running agents.
items.title: NVIDIA, Microsoft Kick Off a New Beginning for Windows PCs with RTX Spark and AI Agents (6 minute read)

items.title: Introducing Playground: Create and play custom games (1 minute read)

items.title: Fired OpenAI Researchers Ask Company to Preserve Visibility Into AI Reasoning (6 minute read)

It also added persistent context, multi-agent orchestration, model routing, governance, and cost controls.

items.summary_html: Hone, a startup formed by a group of former employees from some of the fastest-growing AI firms, has raised a $60 million seed round. The startup aims to create AI agents that can help run a business, essentially serving as professional staffers. These agents will be able to field long-running tasks that run over the course of weeks or even months. The five-month-old startup joins a growing number of companies selling AI software to businesses that promise to automate complex work.
items.title: Former Cognition, Ramp Staffers Want AI Agents Running Businesses (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Epoch Automation Reports show that models can't yet autonomously produce Epoch-quality work. Frontier models performed reliably on well-defined tasks, but they failed in the more open-ended aspects that prevent full automation. Open-weight models lag further behind, struggling even on the well-defined tasks that frontier models handle reliably. The models struggle to pick up Epoch's standards, even with ample reference material, and while they could identify promising research directions, they lacked the judgment to successfully follow through.
items.title: Can AI automate Epoch? (20 minute read)

items.summary_html: Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.
items.title: Why is Speculative Decoding Fast? (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: ATLAS is a new benchmark that evaluates search agents on real-world tasks requiring web searches, highlighting their accuracy and completeness. The benchmark reveals that even high-effort agents miss significant golden answers, indicating major room for improvement in search engines. ATLAS differs from existing benchmarks by focusing on non-memorized tasks, requiring extensive multi-domain searches, and offering a cost-effective grading process.
items.title: ATLAS: Evaluating Agents on Search-Intensive Tasks (13 minute read)

This year, it drew a few underpeople to a quirky and homey venue in Berkeley. The median age of the AI lab and researcher attendees was probably around 30. This post takes a look at the main topics discussed at the conference, which include the debate on whether humans can maintain control of AI technology, whether AI's impact will be good or bad, and how to ensure AI alignment.
items.title: What I saw around the Curve, 2026 (26 minute read)

items.title: How Close Are AI Models to Self-Replication? (28 minute read)

items.summary_html: Cheap-loop domains are domains where experiments are quick, deterministic, and cheap. Expensive-loop domains are restricted by real-world constraints or costs. Most high-value human labor is done in expensive-loop domains. Expensive-loop tasks require the ability to build theories, manage proxies, budget time and compute, and diagnose what went wrong when feedback is scarce, something models don't learn in cheap-loop training.
items.title: The Expensive-Loop Problem (22 minute read)

items.summary_html: Priming is a technique that involves using pretrained Transformer weights to build models with more efficient architectures at less than 1% of the original training cost and with throughputs up to twice as high. It allows researchers to explore the design space, the layer type, the hybrid ratio, and layer placement cheaply and systematically. Every variant starts from the same strong initialization and requires minimal training compared to pretraining. Priming is not tied to a specific Transformer family or model class, and extending it to other models requires no algorithmic changes.
items.title: Can we change an AI model's architecture without retraining it from scratch? (14 minute read)

items.summary_html: On-policy distillation has become increasingly popular for transferring teacher capabilities to student models. Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency. The choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student. OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.
items.title: When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better (1 minute read)

The system utilizes a dual-model software architecture where a vision-language model monitors the environment while a separate model coordinates whole-body manipulation, allowing the robot to dynamically switch tasks. It highlights a major shift toward utilizing integrated foundation models and highly flexible physical platforms to automate complex, multi-step commercial and industrial service roles.
items.title: Dyna-2.1: A Robot/Model for Unsupervised Long-Horizon Workflows (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Kodiak AI is preparing to launch a driverless commercial shipping route for IKEA Supply along a 219-mile section of Interstate 45 in Texas. The milestone follows four years of collaborative testing during which they successfully completed over 1,300 runs to resolve operational complexities like scheduling, predictive maintenance, and dock assignment. It serves as a prime case study of how custom autonomous technology can successfully transition from controlled, simulated environments into the real-world logistics and shipping infrastructure.
items.title: IKEA and Kodiak Prepare for Autonomous Freight Operations (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX's Transporter-18 launched three payloads testing technologies for orbital data centers. Cowboy Space's Reason-1 tests beaming solar power via laser, Google's Project Suncatcher runs AI chips on solar in orbit to evaluate durability, and Star Catcher's Protostar aims to validate power-beaming to satellites. These tests are crucial for building infrastructure to support future AI computing and data centers in space.
items.title: Transporter-18 Tests the Building Blocks of Orbital Data Centers (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: PCIe 8.0 traffic can cross chiplet boundaries through UCIe 3.0, but engineers must coordinate both protocols' power, reset, and recovery states. Timing mismatches can cause completion timeouts, dropped traffic, and deadlocks. Siemens' verification tools trace transactions across both layers and inject faults before silicon bring-up.
items.title: Crossing Chiplet Boundaries With PCIe Over UCIe (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Humanoid robots need different memory architectures for centralized AI compute and distributed joint control. Flash and EEPROM can delay writes by 5-10 milliseconds, which risks lost position data during power failures. The article maps F-RAM to continuous telemetry, safety-capable NOR Flash to boot storage, and high-speed NOR Flash to time-sensitive networking.
items.title: Memory At The Edge: Non-Volatile Memory Challenges And Requirements For Humanoid Robots (8 minute read)

items.summary_html: OpenArm 2.0 is an open-source, 7-degree-of-freedom robotic arm engineered by Tokyo-based Enactic for contact-rich manipulation and physical artificial intelligence research. The arm features backdrivable, quasi-direct drive joints for highly compliant physical interactions, a gripper with an integrated camera, and a motorless replica arm for bilateral force-feedback teleoperation. It delivers a highly customizable, low-cost platform that facilitates the training of robust manipulation models using modern imitation learning and simulation-to-reality pipelines.
items.title: OpenArm 2.0: An Open-Source Compliant Robotic Arm (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Orion is a custom-built, 12-degree-of-freedom quadruped robot designed and programmed entirely from scratch. The system combines an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano for advanced stereo vision depth perception and LiDAR-based SLAM with an STM32-based microcontroller running FreeRTOS for low-level kinematic gaits and real-time stabilization. It provides a complete, open-source blueprint for constructing complex, dynamically stable legged systems using advanced embedded processors and modern spatial computing toolchains.
items.title: Orion: Designing and Programming a Custom Quadruped from Scratch (3 minute read)

The package enables direct control of Lego Spike Prime motors and sensors, allowing developers to run modern robot communication middleware on lightweight educational hardware. It offers an accessible entry point for testing and prototyping mobile bases using popular, modular consumer components.

items.title: Musk confirms TSMC talks on Terafab, which could sideline Intel's 14A node (3 minute read)

The hand, with 13 degrees of freedom, uses dense tactile sensors and enables complex tasks like in-hand object reorientation and tool operation. items.title: Boston Dynamics unveils new four-finger hand for Atlas humanoid robot (4 minute read)

Utilizing AI in patent processes can reduce costs and improve efficiency, crucial for resource-limited startups.
items.title: The physical AI race will be won in the patent office (8 minute read)

items.title: California man charged with smuggling $300M of Nvidia AI servers to China through Malaysia and Singapore (3 minute read)

items.title: Hello Robot awarded $3 million to develop Stretch robot for elder care (5 minute read)

items.title: Nvidia launches a $4,999 DGX Spark with 64GB of memory that clusters with a second unit to run 200B-parameter models (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: GPT-Synopsys is an OpenAI frontier model trained and tuned to operate Synopsys' EDA tools directly, covering PPA optimization, timing closure, and verification. Engineers hand it an objective, and agents run the tools, interpret the results, make changes, and loop until there's a verified outcome to review. It runs on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and plugs into Synopsys.ai and the Autopilot agentic platform. OpenAI licenses Synopsys' tools to train the model, paying a training subscription fee, and the two companies then share revenue based on how well the model improves chip designs, an unusual structure that ties both to the results. Synopsys says customer design data stays protected and won't be used to train the frontier model, and the bundled service covers compute, the model, and EDA licenses.
items.title: Synopsys and OpenAI team up on GPT-Synopsys, a frontier model that runs EDA tools like an engineer (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Engineers must test chips against combined radiation, thermal shock, vibration, and other stresses rather than qualify each condition alone. Arizona State University pairs a radiation source with a cryostat to test devices at 77 Kelvin. Digital twins can model package and system behavior, but physical tests still check whether those predictions hold.
items.title: Designing chips for extreme environments (12 minute read)

items.summary_html: ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability.
items.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM (2 minute read)

The design runs modern quantized language models directly on cost-effective Kintex-7 FPGA PCIe cards, matching simulation results bit for bit. This architecture provides embedded systems designers and compute engineers an invaluable end-to-end reference for deploying and tailoring custom neural network hardware without relying on proprietary black-box tooling.
items.title: OpenTPU Full-Stack Open-Source AI Accelerator (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: Anduril will invest $3.7 billion to build a two-million-square-foot "software-defined" shipyard at Sparrows Point, the former Bethlehem Steel site near Baltimore, and the Navy separately awarded it a $2.9 billion "Arsenal 2" contract with payments tied to production outcomes, bringing the package to roughly $6.6 billion.
items.title: Trump announces nearly $7B Anduril submarine shipyard deal in Baltimore (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: TSMC reported revenue of $511.86 billion New Taiwan dollars for September, a 54.6% year-over-year increase. Demand for advanced AI chips, driven by customers like Nvidia and Apple, boosted sales. TSMC has also committed to using ASML's advanced lithography machines to enhance chip production.
items.title: TSMC's September sales surge year-over-year as AI drives chip demand (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: Amazon built its 1,000th Leo broadband satellite at its Kirkland, Washington plant, which took six months to produce its first 27 and now turns out 27 a week. It builds propulsion in-house and borrowed consumer electronics methods to cut tests that took weeks down to hours. The bottleneck is launch: only 396 are in orbit against 3,232 needed, and the Vulcan grounding and a New Glenn pad explosion cost Amazon FCC spectrum priority.
items.title: Amazon builds its 1,000th Leo satellite at 27 a week, but only 396 are in orbit (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: IEEE Spectrum examines the up-to-$1B CHIPS R&D award finalized for IBM spinoff Anderon in September. IBM is matching that funding with $1B, while Anderon uses a 300mm Albany line and plans foundry services and process design kits for outside developers. The challenge is repeatable fabrication, including tighter control of Josephson junctions, rather than simply adding wafer capacity.
items.title: Anderon aims to industrialize quantum chip fabrication (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Tensor virtualization decouples a tensor's logical layout from its physical GPU allocation, so one shader template replaces separate backend-specific codebases. For edge LLMs, ML Drift switches kernels between compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode, using a convolution-aligned KV cache layout and in-kernel activation quantization to skip memory roundtrips. It cut YouTube Shorts frame latency by up to 40%, and Google co-optimized it with Arm, Intel, and Qualcomm GPUs.
items.title: Google open-sources ML Drift, a GPU engine that runs one shader set across OpenCL, Metal, WebGPU, and OpenGL ES (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: Scientists from the Harbin Institute of Technology developed a cement-based supercapacitor capable of powering small devices like LEDs. The device uses a 3D-printed electrode ink made from carbon nanotubes and cement, enabling fast energy discharge. Future research will enhance cold-weather performance, potentially allowing buildings to store energy and support smart environments.
items.title: Supercapacitor cement is key to buildings that store their own power (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Gartner predicts that over half of quantum startups will fail by 2030 due to a market unable to generate sufficient revenue. Despite this, companies are investing in quantum technologies for their potential business advantages, focusing on building expertise rather than waiting for technological maturity. The public sector and financial industries are expected to lead quantum computing investments, with spending reaching $245 million and $289 million by 2027 and 2028, respectively.
items.title: Too many quantum startups, too little money to keep them alive (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Apple gained a full percentage point in market share year-over-year as RAM price increases led to a 20% decrease in overall PC shipments. Despite this downturn, Apple was less affected than most competitors. With prices expected to worsen, Apple's resilience highlights its strong customer base willing to invest in new devices.
items.title: There's a hidden upside to the rampocalypse for Apple (1 minute read)

items.summary_html: NVIDIA expanded its Halos safety system from self-driving cars to robots with Halos for Robotics in June.
items.title: NVIDIA's Safety Stack for Physical AI (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: The toolchain covers synthetic data generation, training, simulation and validation, edge deployment, and continuous improvement.
items.title: AWS Launches an Open-Source Physical AI Toolchain for Robotics (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: Microsoft's 15-inch Surface Laptop Ultra runs Nvidia's RTX Spark superchip, pairing up to a 20-core Grace CPU and Blackwell graphics with up to 128GB of unified memory, enough for local agents on models up to 120B parameters.
items.title: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra brings Nvidia's RTX Spark to a 15-inch, $2,600 laptop (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Who's building on-prem compute in 2026? It turns out a lot of people! Oxide Computer Company, which builds custom on-prem cloud compute systems, has closed a massive $445 million Series D funding round led by Eclipse, with participation from major investors including Jane Street, Atreides Management, and chipmaker AMD. The capital injection follows the startup achieving operational profitability and will be used to scale manufacturing capacity, secure raw material inventory, and fulfill a rapidly expanding order backlog for their commercial cloud computer racks.
items.title: Oxide Computer Company Secures $445M Series D Funding Round (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: SpaceX agreed to buy up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz low-band spectrum, which penetrates buildings, and plans to deploy its own antennas on towers and rooftops to use it, with most existing phones already supporting the band. Separately, the FCC approved 15,000 more Starlink satellites optimized for 2 GHz. Together they point to a hybrid network, terrestrial indoors and satellite beyond towers. The deal needs FCC approval, and Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile shares fell roughly 6% on the news.
items.title: SpaceX buys 800 MHz low-band spectrum to pair terrestrial towers with 2 GHz Starlink satellites (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: In this rare peek under the hood, we get a glimpse of how Foxconn uses NVIDIA Omniverse, Isaac, and Metropolis platforms to create physically accurate digital twins of manufacturing facilities that assemble next-generation AI server hardware. By simulating factory layouts, automated optical inspection systems, and autonomous mobile robot fleets in virtual environments before physical deployment, the company minimizes factory commissioning delays and boosts production efficiency. This approach showcases how system architects and automation specialists can leverage high-fidelity simulation to safely validate and optimize complex robotic workcells prior to hardware installation.
items.title: The Machines That Make the Machines: Advancing Industrial Digital Twins (5 minute read)

items.summary_html: After May's pad explosion destroyed its transporter-erector, Blue Origin is rebuilding LC-36 for vertical integration, loading New Glenn through the support tower alone, as with Starship. Crews destacked the tower, added cryogenic propellant plumbing on the ground, and have begun restacking modules, while the launch bridge is restored. Umbilicals and fairing access platforms haven't appeared yet. Bezos targets a December return to flight carrying Blue Ring, though he joked it could slip to December 31.
items.title: Blue Origin rebuilds LC-36 for vertical New Glenn integration, targeting a December return (4 minute read)

items.summary_html: A Nature Computational Science briefing describes an in situ learning method where photonic integrated circuits directly measure optical gradients, so diverse circuit layouts can be trained after they're built. That removes the need for a full digital model of the chip, which optical training normally leans on. The team demonstrated matrix design, multiwavelength computation, and rapid meta-learning on the hardware. Specifics like accuracy or energy figures aren't included.
items.title: Photonic chips learn after fabrication by measuring their own optical gradients (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: ScaRF-SLAM is a dense visual mapping system that pairs the reliability of classical visual SLAM with modern feed-forward geometric foundation models for 3D scene reconstruction from the Oxford Robot Dynamics Lab. By decoupling camera tracking from dense depth estimation and optimizing scale consistency across submaps, it achieves globally accurate 3D maps across diverse sensor configurations. For perception engineers and autonomy developers, this framework provides a practical way to produce metric-scale environmental maps in real time without sacrificing tracking stability
items.title: ScaRF-SLAM: Scale-Consistent Reconstruction with Feed-Forward Models and Classical Visual SLAM (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: ZeroWire Robotics has launched the Q8botOne, a smartphone-sized open-source quadruped robot featuring an innovative wire-free chassis where the main printed circuit board serves as the structural frame. Driven by an ESP32-C3 microcontroller and eight DYNAMIXEL smart bus actuators with parallel-linkage legs, the compact robot can walk, trot, jump, and carry twice its 250-gram payload.
items.title: Q8botOne: A Palm-Sized Open-Source Quadruped Robot with Smart Actuators (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ledger confirmed an unauthorized hardware implant in one affected user's device, bought from Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis, pointing to tampering after manufacturing rather than a breach of Ledger itself. Mark Karpelès published images of a modified Nano X with a small board behind the screen and cellular components, which would presumably capture the 24-word recovery phrase as it displays during setup, leaving the secure element untouched.
items.title: Ledger confirms a hardware implant in a tampered wallet as suspected losses near $93M (3 minute read)

items.summary_html: Ting-Wei Sun pleaded guilty to four counts, including conspiracy to violate export controls, in a scheme that routed about $2.5 billion of Nvidia-powered servers through a Southeast Asian company to buyers in China.
items.title: Super Micro “fixer” pleads guilty in $2.5B scheme to divert Nvidia servers to China (3 minute read)

items.title: ASML raises EUV and DUV spare parts prices 10% for Samsung and SK Hynix (3 minute read)

items.title: Jumper: An Open-Source Crab Robot with Walking and Jumping Capabilities (2 minute read)

items.summary_html: EasyNav 0.5.0 has officially launched, delivering an accessible yet comprehensive open-source navigation stack with upgraded path planning, improved recovery behaviors, and reduced compute overhead for ROS 2 systems.
items.title: EasyNav 0.5.0 Navigation System Released for ROS 2 Distributions (2 minute read)
